measures.what_it_does: Makes the county ambulance district's property tax levy permanent, at up to $0.50 per $1,000 of assessed value, starting with 2027 collection. Voters renewed the levy for six years in 2018 and 2024; this removes the end date and the need for future renewal votes. The money may be spent only on emergency medical services. The district covers the county except the Bickleton area. State law calls for 60% approval for a permanent levy; the district's resolution says a simple majority.
measures.cost_line: Up to $0.50 per $1,000 of assessed value every year with no end date: about $250 a year on a $500,000 property at the full rate. The 2026 rate under the current levy is about $0.48, raising $2.56 million.
measures.pro_summary: No statement in favor was filed. The district says the levy pays for its ambulances, facilities, equipment and trained emergency medical personnel; in 2024 it described about 2,417 911 responses a year across 1,400 square miles.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposing committee is listed. A permanent levy ends the six-year re-votes that voters have approved twice with about 74%; state law requires a referendum procedure for permanent levies (15% of voters can petition), which the district's resolution does not mention.

taxes.basis: A yes vote keeps the existing EMS levy at the same $0.50 maximum but with no end date. It is a continuation of a tax voters approved in 2018 and 2024, not a new or higher one.

measures.sources_note: Sources: the local voters' pamphlet page 56 (S1); EMS District Resolution 2026-02 (S2); VoteWA records for 2026 and 2024 (S3, S4); the Assessor's 2026 levy report (S5); RCW 84.52.069 (S6); SOS results for 2024 and 2018 (S7, S8); the Auditor's 2025 votes by district (S9); a district-written Sentinel column (S10). No news coverage of the 2026 measure was found.
